stem: The student wants to describe the method Haskó used in her study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Wetlands along the Vellin River support dozens of dragonfly species.
• Ecologist Mirela Haskó wanted to know whether beaver dams affect how many dragonfly species live in these wetlands.
• She counted dragonfly larvae in 24 ponds: 12 behind beaver dams and 12 with no dams.
• Ponds behind beaver dams held nearly twice as many dragonfly species as undammed ponds.
• Haskó concluded that beavers create the slow-moving water that many dragonflies need.
choices: Haskó wanted to know whether beaver dams affect how many dragonfly species live in the wetlands along the Vellin River.
To study the question, Haskó counted dragonfly larvae in 24 ponds, 12 of them behind beaver dams and 12 with no dams.
Haskó found that ponds behind beaver dams held nearly twice as many dragonfly species as ponds that had no dams.
Haskó concluded that beavers help dragonflies by creating the slow-moving water that many of the insects need.
explanation: The goal asks for one stage of the study: the method. Only B tells you what Haskó actually did, counting larvae in 24 ponds split between dammed and undammed sites. The other choices give the study's aim, result, or conclusion.

A.why: You picked the study's aim, the question Haskó asked, but the goal asks how she went about answering it. This choice names Haskó's study but describes the wrong stage of it.

C.why: You picked the study's finding, probably because it is the most interesting note. The goal asks for the method, and this sentence gives the result.

D.why: You picked Haskó's conclusion. It's accurate, but it explains what the results mean instead of describing how the study was done.

stem: The student wants to describe where the Lantern fossil was discovered. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Harlow Ridge fossil collection contains more than 300 plant specimens.
• Most of the specimens are ferns and horsetails roughly 300 million years old.
• One specimen, a fossil seed cone nicknamed "Lantern," is the oldest in the collection.
• Lantern was found in 1987 in a coal seam beneath a farm in Brenner County.
• The cone's scales are preserved in enough detail that each one can be counted.
choices: The Harlow Ridge collection, which includes Lantern, holds more than 300 plant specimens, mostly ferns and horsetails.
Lantern, the oldest specimen in the Harlow Ridge fossil collection, is a seed cone from an ancient plant.
Lantern was discovered in 1987 in a coal seam lying beneath a farm in Brenner County.
Lantern's scales are preserved in such fine detail that researchers can count each one.
explanation: The goal ends with "where the Lantern fossil was discovered," and only one note answers that: a coal seam beneath a Brenner County farm. Choice C makes that location the main point of the sentence.

A.why: You picked a sentence about the whole collection. Lantern appears only in a side clause, and the sentence never says where it was found.

B.why: This choice names Lantern but describes what it is and how old it is, not where it was found. Having the right name in a sentence doesn't make it the right detail.

D.why: You picked a feature of the fossil, its well-preserved scales. That's a real detail about Lantern, but it isn't the discovery site.

stem: The student wants to describe how the Kestrel variety copes with dry conditions. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Dunmore Plant Breeding Station has released three sorghum varieties since 2010.
• Amberline (2011) was bred for high grain yield in irrigated fields.
• Kestrel (2015) has roots that reach nearly two meters deep, allowing it to draw water during dry spells.
• Copperhead (2019) resists a fungal leaf disease common in humid regions.
choices: Since 2010, the Dunmore Plant Breeding Station has released three sorghum varieties, one of which is Kestrel.
Released four years after Kestrel, the Copperhead variety resists a fungal leaf disease common in humid regions.
Amberline, released four years before Kestrel, was bred to produce high grain yields in irrigated fields.
Kestrel, released in 2015, has roots nearly two meters deep that let it draw water during dry spells.
explanation: The goal names one variety (Kestrel) and one feature (how it handles dry conditions). Choice D makes Kestrel the subject and tells you its deep roots let it reach water during dry spells.

A.why: You picked a sentence about the whole set of varieties. It mentions Kestrel but says nothing about how Kestrel handles drought.

B.why: This choice mentions Kestrel, but its subject is Copperhead and its disease resistance. Here the right name only serves as a date reference for a different variety.

C.why: This choice uses Kestrel only as a reference point and describes Amberline, a variety bred for irrigated fields, not for dry ones.

stem: The student wants to describe the earthquake activity the network recorded before the 2019 Ardley earthquake. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Saltmarsh Seismic Network was installed along the Corrin Fault in 2009.
• From 2009 to 2018, its sensors recorded an average of 40 small earthquakes per year.
• In 2019, a magnitude 5.1 earthquake struck near the town of Ardley.
• In the year after the Ardley earthquake, the network recorded more than 600 aftershocks.
• Since 2021, the network's data have been shared publicly online.
choices: From 2009 to 2018, the Saltmarsh Seismic Network recorded an average of 40 small earthquakes per year.
In the year after the 2019 Ardley earthquake, the Saltmarsh Seismic Network recorded more than 600 aftershocks.
The Saltmarsh Seismic Network was installed along the Corrin Fault in 2009, ten years before the Ardley earthquake.
Since 2021, data from the Saltmarsh Seismic Network, which recorded the Ardley earthquake, have been shared online.
explanation: The goal limits you to a time period (before 2019) and one thing (recorded earthquake activity). Choice A gives the activity the network recorded from 2009 to 2018, which is the full span before the Ardley earthquake.

B.why: This choice describes recorded earthquake activity, but from the wrong period: the year after Ardley. The goal says "before," and you skipped that restriction.

C.why: This choice falls in the right time period, but it tells you when and where the network was installed, not what earthquakes it recorded.

D.why: You picked a sentence about how the network's data are shared now. It doesn't describe any earthquake activity before 2019.

stem: The student wants to describe the materials used to make the Orchard Coverlet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Penhallow Museum holds four coverlets woven in the 1840s by Thomasina Reyle.
• Reyle learned to weave from her aunt in a mill town in northern England.
• Her best-known coverlet, the Orchard Coverlet, is woven from linen and indigo-dyed wool.
• The Orchard Coverlet's border shows a repeating pattern of apple trees.
• Reyle's later coverlets were woven with cotton bought from local mills.
choices: Reyle, the weaver of the Orchard Coverlet, learned her craft from an aunt in a northern English mill town.
The border of the Orchard Coverlet, Reyle's best-known work, displays a repeating pattern of apple trees.
The Orchard Coverlet, Reyle's best-known work, is woven from linen and from wool dyed with indigo.
Reyle's later coverlets, made after the Orchard Coverlet, were woven with cotton bought from local mills.
explanation: The goal names one textile, the Orchard Coverlet, and one aspect of it: its materials. Choice C makes the coverlet the subject and names its materials, linen and indigo-dyed wool.

A.why: You picked the weaver's biography. The coverlet is named, but the sentence is about how Reyle learned to weave, not what the coverlet is made of.

B.why: This choice is about the right coverlet but describes its design, not its materials.

D.why: This choice does name a material, but it belongs to Reyle's later coverlets, not the Orchard Coverlet. You matched the topic of materials but not the item the goal names.
